text: When you design a REST API, clear structure matters. Start by naming your endpoints in a simple, logical way, using nouns that describe the resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation is essential, because other developers need to know how to use your endpoints without guessing. Finally, plan for versioning from the beginning—for example, by adding /v1/ to your URLs—so you can improve the API without breaking existing applications.
